correctness.rationale: Let u>=3, j=2^u, r=j+u, M=2^r, N=M-j-1. For S_N=sum_{k=1}^N2^k/k in Q_2, both infinite log sum_{k>=1}2^k/k and dilog sum_{k>=1}2^k/k^2 vanish by 2-adic log(-1)=0 and Li_2(z)+Li_2(z/(z-1))=-log^2(1-z)/2 at z=2. Normalize -S_N as its tail by 2^(M-r). Endpoint k=M-j and k=M terms cancel to valuation j. Replacing intermediate (M-a)^(-1) by -a^(-1) has valuation >=3u-1 error; geometric expansion gives sum_{s>=1}2^(us)H_s. The s=1,2 layers vanish below j by full-series tails; s=3 has unique minimum b=4 with v2(2^b/b^3)=-2, giving 3u-2, while all s>=4 and endpoints remain >=3u-1. Hence v2(S_N)=M-r+3u-2. The known identity a_N=(N!/2^N)S_N and Legendre v2(N!/2^N)=-s2(N)=-(r-1) give v2(a_N)=M-2r+3u-1. Independent modular tail checks u=3..8 and full recurrence N=2039 match; finite tests are not the infinite proof.
